items.blurb: Staff: latest stable is 0.24.0; no public changelog yet (Settings → Updates plus X); there is no official Debian/Fedora desktop app.

items.name: Grok Bot hanging at Cleaning up after reset
items.blurb: Staff: the reset usually finishes on the backend; the dialog just misses the done signal at Cleaning up. Fully quit and reopen, then Recover — don’t Reset again.

items.name: Grok Bot 0.24.0 Windows white flash then the app closes
items.blurb: Staff: the cloud computer was healthy; a white flash then the process dying is usually local (endpoint security, locked %APPDATA%, or a partial install), not GPU.

items.name: Bots workspace looks empty after a rebuild
items.blurb: Staff: after a rebuild, logging in while the computer is still starting can show first-run UI; bots are not gone. Fully quit and reopen, and don’t create your first bot in that window.

items.name: No compact / new session; full transcript is sent each turn
items.blurb: Staff: desktop and iOS have no explicit Compact or same-bot new session. Auto-summary is not compact; the full transcript is sent, and there is no model picker.

items.name: Overbooked then Bot failed to respond is model load
items.blurb: Staff: “overbooked” then “Bot failed to respond” is service-side Grok model load, not your account, usage, or computer; wait for a quieter window or reset again.

items.name: Black screen after setup: hosted computer never finished starting
items.blurb: Staff: black screen after “Setting up Grok Bot’s computer” means the hosted computer never finished starting; reinstall will not help, and if the same account still works on iOS do not Reset (that drops bots)—wait for a staff rebuild.

items.name: 0.27.0 Windows: local host stays disconnected after clean registration
items.blurb: Staff: on 0.27.0 Windows the agent can say the local machine isn’t connected even after a clean daemon registration; fully quit every Grok process and launch once, and if it still fails it is service-side.

items.name: Webhook URL and sender key are desktop-only, not on iOS
items.blurb: Staff: a webhook routine’s POST URL and sender key only appear on the Grok Bot desktop app, not iOS; open the trigger card there (keep the desktop app updated).

items.name: Official X plugin auth is broken on desktop, Cloud, and Grok Bot
items.blurb: Staff: official X plugin connect/refresh is failing across desktop, Cloud Agents, and Grok Bot (including “connected but tools=0”); no clean workaround while they fix X-side app config.

items.name: Weekly Grok Bot usage can spill into paid On-Demand with no warning
items.blurb: Staff: spend order is Grok Bot weekly allowance, then referral/promo credits, then paid On-Demand, with no in-app warning; a $0 On-Demand cap does not block credits, so pause near 100% weekly meter if you want no spill.

items.name: Pro weekly pool is separate; overflow hits shared On-Demand
items.blurb: Staff correction: on Pro, Grok Bot has its own included weekly pool, separate from Cursor plan usage; overflow still bills the shared On-Demand pool, so set a $0 On-Demand cap if you want no paid spill.

items.name: Access is live for paid plans, not legacy request-based
items.blurb: Staff: Grok Bot is live for all paid individual plans (Pro / Pro+ / Ultra) and self-serve Teams with no percent or region rollout; legacy request-based pricing does not get it unless you opt into usage-based.

items.name: Gmail plugin OAuth is broken; authorize from Cursor
items.blurb: Staff: the Grok Bot Gmail plugin OAuth is broken; authorizing Gmail from Cursor uses a different path and the connection is shared with Grok Bot until the plugin is fixed.

items.name: iOS 1.3.2 sends a question list on the first tap
items.blurb: Staff: iOS 1.3.2 sends a question list as soon as you tap one option; multi-select before send needs a newer Grok Bot app build.

items.name: Grok-launched agents hide behind the Source filter
items.blurb: Staff: Grok-launched cloud agents do appear on cursor.com/agents — enable the Source → Grok Bot filter; middle-click “Open in Cursor” opens the same agent in the browser.

items.name: Days-long “Can’t reach your computer” needs a staff restore
items.blurb: Staff: a days-long “Can’t reach your computer” can be a stuck hosted box that Reset / Recover / reinstall cannot clear; staff restores it on their side, then fully quit and reopen the app.

items.name: Fresh-install white screen is a local profile, not the cloud box
items.blurb: Staff: a fresh-install white window is a local profile bug, not a stuck cloud computer; fully quit, rename ~/Library/Application Support/Grok Bot to Grok Bot.bak, then relaunch — reinstall alone will not clear it.

items.name: Grok-spawned Cloud Agents can ignore your non-Fast default
items.blurb: Staff: Grok-spawned Cursor Cloud Agents can start in Fast even when your default is not; hover Cursor Grok 4.6 → Edit and uncheck Fast, and switch the follow-up box back if it flips.

items.name: Local execution offline while chat still works
items.blurb: Staff: the local-exec helper can register then drop its server link, so the Mac shows offline while chat still works; fully quit and reopen, and if it fails again send ~/.grokbot/local-exec-daemon.log.

items.name: Reset stuck at 50% Starting is a server-side bad state
items.blurb: Staff: a Reset hung at 50% “Starting Grok Bot’s computer” is a bad hosted state, not your install; Bot data is not lost — wait a few minutes, and reply on the thread if it still fails.

items.name: Local CLI orchestration and always-allow are intended use
items.blurb: Staff: local-CLI orchestration (including Cursor CLI), always-allow local execution, and authenticated browser sessions are intended Grok Bot use; third-party ToS stay separate, bots share one computer, and a continuous Pro orchestrator burns the weekly pool fast.

items.name: Local-computer helper fails registration
items.blurb: Staff: the local-computer helper can start then fail registration after an update; full-quit plus sign-out recreates it, and desktop 0.31.0 is rolling out.

items.name: Mac black screen is local DNS not cloud
items.blurb: Staff: Mac 0.30.0 black screen with working iOS bots is a local network/DNS block to the healthy cloud computer, not a recreate-computer problem.

items.name: Grok Bot does not spend Pro $20 IDE credit
items.blurb: Staff: Pro’s $20 Other Models credit is not Grok Bot’s weekly pool; dashboard “Included in Pro” is shared billing — and with On-Demand off the Bot can still drain Cursor credits (referral/promo) before stopping (see 169982).

items.name: Does GrokBot not have access to my Cursor Codebase?
items.blurb: Staff: Grok Bot has no codebase plugin and does not index your repo; coding work is handed to a Cursor Cloud Agent on a GitHub-connected account (Dashboard → Integrations), with an optional GitHub PAT connector for read-only, auto-created repos from scratch, and no Origin access yet.

items.name: Phantom in Grok Bot is a Mess
items.blurb: Staff: the Phantom plugin runs on @phantom/mcp-server and each new auth creates a separate dedicated agent wallet, not your personal Phantom wallet, so reconnects show a new address while funded funds stay on the old agent wallet (recover via chat history or Phantom Support).

items.name: Grokbot custom connectors
items.blurb: Staff: there is no settings form for custom connectors; tell the Bot in chat to add an MCP server (public HTTPS streamable HTTP/SSE), confirm the details, and new tools appear from the next message — localhost-only MCP on your PC is unreachable from the cloud computer.

items.name: Grok Bot: Drive MCP should write Google Docs body and Sheet cells, not only file metadata
items.blurb: Staff: in-place Google Doc/Sheet editing lives in the dedicated Docs and Sheets connectors (edit content against the existing file ID), while Drive is file-level only; add both from the connector marketplace with the same Google account.

items.name: Blank screen after opening Grok Bot
items.blurb: Staff: a blank/white screen usually means the desktop app cannot reach the cloud computer; Cloudflare WARP can intercept that traffic even on a hotspot — turn WARP off or use split tunneling/excluded routes, and prefer builds after 0.28.0 that show an error+retry instead of a blank screen.

items.name: Cloud Agents created in Grok Bot not displayed in Cursor
items.blurb: Staff: Cloud Agents launched from Grok Bot keep running under your account but stay hidden on cursor.com/agents and the desktop sidebar until you enable filter Source > Grok Bot (once per client: web and desktop).

items.name: Can't reach your computer from last 72 hours
items.blurb: Staff: when the cloud computer is healthy but the app still says Can’t reach, set both IPv4 and IPv6 DNS to 1.1.1.1/8.8.8.8 (JioFiber routers often keep IPv6 DNS) or confirm via a phone hotspot on another carrier.

items.name: Grok Bot 0.30.0 stuck on "Setting up your Grok Bot" on macOS
items.blurb: Staff: endless Setting up your Grok Bot on a free Cursor plan means no hosted machine is provisioned — needs Pro/Pro+/Ultra/Teams or linked SuperGrok/Plus/Heavy; the spinner instead of an access message is a known UX bug.

items.name: Grok Bot Zoom plugin OAuth hardcodes http://localhost:8787/callback — Zoom rejects hostname localhost (error 4700)
items.blurb: Staff: the catalog Zoom plugin OAuth hardcodes http://localhost:8787/callback, which Zoom rejects (error 4700); no user workaround until the redirect moves off localhost (e.g. 127.0.0.1).

items.name: Unable to reconnect to my Grok Bot's computer after attempted update
items.blurb: Staff: bots/files/logins live on the remote computer; Can’t Reach plus failed Recover/Reset often means a lost app login session — fully quit, sign out/in (or reinstall and sign in), since Recover/Reset need a working session.

items.name: Grok Bot Computer Stuck in Partial State — Reset Failed, Existing Cloud Computer Unreachable
items.blurb: Staff: hold off on Reset/Recover after a scary partial-state dialog — data is remote and failed resets often failed on the app side; re-login, verify via mobile on cellular, and try public DNS / disable VPN before resetting.

items.name: Grok Bot couldn't finish setup
items.blurb: Staff: Can’t reach your computer on Linux Grok Bot 0.18.0 is not your network — Grok Bot is not officially available on Linux yet and that old build is rejected; supported platforms are macOS, Windows, and iOS.

items.name: Grok Bot 0.30.0 (Windows) — setup fails with Can't reach your computer, all network checks pass
items.blurb: Staff: the app reaches a per-computer subdomain under cursorvm.com, not the apex — if nslookup test123.us8.cursorvm.com is Query refused while the apex works, change DNS on both IPv4 and IPv6 (router RA can keep the ISP resolver even after 1.1.1.1).

items.name: Grok Bot draining Cursor credit pool
items.blurb: Staff: after the Grok Bot weekly pool on Pro+ is gone, usage keeps going onto Cursor credits (referral/promo) first, then on-demand if enabled; a $0 on-demand cap stops paid overage but not credit drain, and claude-opus / grok-4.6-high-fast lines are models the Bot picks server-side.

items.name: Grok Bot templates: preview shows skills, but the export ships skills: [] — skills are never delivered
items.blurb: Staff: Bot template preview lists skills, but import does not apply them (export ships skills: []); until that is fixed, copy the skill body from the preview and ask the new Bot to recreate it.

items.name: Cloud computer wipes packages after rebuild
items.blurb: Staff: Update Computer keeps files and logins but rebuilds the OS image, so apt/apps/daemons are gone; the box also sleeps when idle (background processes die) and can auto-update during idle — keep a package list in a file and ask the Bot to reinstall after an update.

items.name: /review-bugbot is missing on cloud agents launched from Grok Bot
items.blurb: Staff: /review and /review-bugbot do not attach to cloud agents created by Grok Bot (decided at create time); start a new agent from cursor.com/agents on the same PR branch and include /review-bugbot there.

items.name: Grok Bot Bug Report (empty roster / black screen after reconnect)
items.blurb: Staff: empty bot list and black/white loading after reconnect usually means the Agent Computer was slow waking from sleep—nothing deleted; do not Reset; fully quit and relaunch once the box is awake.

items.name: Grokbot and GitHub (Connected but Authorization header badly formatted)
items.blurb: Staff: GitHub connector shows Connected but fails with “Authorization header is badly formatted”—tracked bug; workaround is press-and-hold the account → Remove, then reconnect and sign in again.

items.name: Authorization death by 1000 clicks
items.blurb: Staff: “Always allow” for local-computer actions lives only in the desktop app on that machine; iOS can only one-time-approve, and those approvals clear on every new message—set Always Allow under desktop Settings → Execution on Local Computer.

items.name: Wrangler/box auth reminder stays stuck after auth already succeeded via another path
items.blurb: Staff: the “help on its computer” / Waiting-for-you reminder only clears when you answer that card (“I’m done, continue” or Skip) or send any chat message—it does not auto-dismiss if the Bot finished login another way.

items.name: Fastmail Filters & Rules Save is a silent no-op (Chrome on the box)
items.blurb: Staff: Fastmail Settings → Filters & Rules Save on the box Chrome fires zero network requests; workaround is manage filters/Sieve via Fastmail’s API (JMAP) with a token—the mail helper already uses that path successfully.

items.name: VPN, SSO, Passkey, and YubiKey Within Grokbot
items.blurb: Staff: Grok Bot’s cloud computer cannot join a corporate VPN today (don’t install a VPN client on it — that can knock the box offline); Atlassian Cloud / public SSO works via browser takeover (Okta etc.), YubiKey works on macOS/Windows under Settings → Security Key, and internal VPN-only sites need Execution on Local Computer on your VPN’d machine.

items.name: Unable to connect
items.blurb: Staff: chats and agents live on the hosted Grok Bot computer — during an outage recovery that computer can be temporarily replaced with a blank one (roster looks empty); Cursor can restore it from saved data, then quit and reopen the app to see agents/history again.

items.name: GrokBot Linux Execution on Local Computer not working
items.blurb: Staff: empty ListMachines / local execution failing on Grok Bot 0.30.0 Linux is a known bug with a fix already merged for the next desktop update; interim workaround is an unlocked system keyring (gnome-keyring or KWallet), fully quit leftover Grok Bot processes, then relaunch.

items.name: New report, Windows, leftover daemon on 0.30.0
items.blurb: Staff: 0.30.0 fixed one macOS daemon exit/no-respawn path, but Windows leftover local-exec-daemon is a different known failure; when the machine is unreachable, Quit from the tray, end remaining “Grok Bot” and local-exec-daemon processes in Task Manager, relaunch, and wait about a minute to re-register.

items.name: Grok bot failed to respond
items.blurb: Staff (kevinn): “Bot failed to respond” on every bot—including fresh copies—means the shared cloud computer is stuck, not something you can fix by restarting or recreating bots; after staff recovery, fully quit (Cmd+Q / force-close iOS), update every install, keep one open, and test in a new chat.

items.name: Grok Bot 0.30.0 Stuck on Black Loading Screen During Initial Setup on Mac
items.blurb: Staff (Colin): Team admin role alone does not provision a Grok Bot computer — Grok Bot is included with a paid team seat (Standard or Premium), not the admin role. If the signed-in account has no seat, the app sits on the black loading screen with no computer to reset. Fix: assign yourself a seat in Cursor dashboard Members, fully quit and reopen Grok Bot; or sign in with a seated team account.

items.name: Grok Bot: weekly usage hits 100% after bot-to-bot reviews the user asked to stop
items.blurb: Staff (mohitjain): Each bot-to-bot message burns a weekly-usage turn; asking bots in chat to “stay quiet” is only a hint. Reliable fixes: run work in one Command Agent with subagents (they finish and stop), and delete unused specialist bots (idle bots can still be woken; deleting also clears that bot’s chat — save first). Double limit banners are blocked retries, not double charges.

items.name: Grok Bot Windows — fresh profile setup fails with “Can’t reach your computer” after backend fix
items.blurb: Staff (deanrie): Grok Bot ignores the Windows system proxy / local HTTP proxy and connects direct to the Agent Computer — so DNS/TCP/CONNECT checks through a proxy can pass while the app fails. Use VPN/proxy TUN (Enhanced/Global/virtual adapter) mode, then verify with curl.exe --noproxy "*" -I https://test123.<region>.cursorvm.com (expect 404 awselb/2.0). User confirmed TUN fixed setup. Region may be us10 not us8.

items.name: Grok Bot 0.30.0 stuck on black loading screen on Windows 11
items.blurb: Staff (Colin): Healthy cloud computer + black spinner on both LAN and hotspot can be Zscaler Client Connector still tunneling (including on hotspot). Quit Grok Bot, pause/disable Zscaler, relaunch; ask IT to allowlist/exclude SSL inspection for *.cursorvm.com and **.cursorvm.com (both levels).

items.name: Grok Bot cannot attach inline images to Cursor bug reports (chat drop and forum upload)
items.blurb: Staff (mohitjain): To get a screenshot into Grok Bot chat, use the composer + button (or drag a saved file) and wait for the thumbnail before send — drag-from-browser/other-app or Enter-before-thumbnail usually drops it. Forum upload by the assistant is a current limitation; attach the screenshot yourself or reply to support email.

items.name: Grok Bot routines don't auto-run on schedule
items.blurb: Staff (Colin): Editing bot instructions or which platform created a routine does not break schedules — late “Next run: Run now” usually means the slot fired but sat in a queue (often 10–37 min), and some runs finish without posting to chat; don’t recreate routines; message the bot for an on-demand check-in.

items.name: Grok Bot 0.30.0 — Agent Computer unreachable after Update, Recover, and Reset all failed
items.blurb: Staff (kevinn): An “Aw, Snap!” Chrome page on the Bot screen after idle wake is the Bot’s browser crashing inside a healthy computer — reload the tab or ask the Bot to reload, fully quit/reopen Grok Bot if needed, and do not run Update/Recover/Reset; idle machines take a moment to wake and a first message can miss, so resend is safe.

items.name: Grok Bot Mac “unavailable” after password reset (expired session)
items.blurb: Staff (deanrie): After a password reset, Grok Bot on Mac can keep an expired session and show “isn’t available on this account yet” even though SuperGrok/Cursor access and your cloud computer/Bots are fine — Log out from the bottom of that screen, fully Quit (Cmd+Q), reopen and Sign in with the new password; Check Access→download is a misleading expired-session UI, not a missing entitlement.

items.name: Homepage “Approval needed” stuck after card timeout
items.blurb: Staff (Colin): A homepage “Approval needed” tile with nothing pending usually means an approval card timed out (~10 minutes unanswered); open the agent and send a short message or restart the app to clear a stuck badge — the tile is supposed to clear when the card expires.

items.name: File contents and grokbot — viewer Copy vs Download
items.blurb: Staff (Colin): The in-app file viewer only offers Download today; for .md/.txt you can click-drag to select and Cmd/Ctrl+C, while .docx/.pdf won’t highlight — ask the Bot to paste the full text into chat and use the message Copy action as a workaround.

items.name: Grok Bot Canva connector failing — Invalid redirect URI on iOS
items.blurb: Staff (deanrie): Canva “Invalid redirect URI” on Grok Bot iOS 1.4.0 is a known app-link vs web-redirect mismatch (not your Canva settings) — connect Canva from desktop Grok Bot on the same account and the connector syncs to iPhone.

items.name: Local computer looks connected but CopyFromBox/Shell flaps after large transfer timeout
items.blurb: Staff (deanrie): A large CopyFromBox (or timed-out Shell) can drop the local machine from the agent list for ~1 minute while Settings still says connected — split big copies, wait a minute before retrying, and if stuck Cmd+Q then pkill -f local-exec-daemon and reopen.
